newsitem.title: USA: Millstone outages could cause Q4 NU loss.
newsitem.headline: Millstone outages could cause Q4 NU loss.

text.p: Northeast Utilities's costs related to the outages of the Millstone nuclear power plants could result in a fourth quarter loss, the company said in its third quarter Form 10-Q filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Northeast Utilities reported earnings of $64.2 million, or $0.50 per share, in 1995's final quarter. The First Call consensus estimate for the current quarter is $0.04 per share.
Assuming normal weather conditions, the 10Q said, NU management expects the system would have sufficient capacity to meet peak load demands even if nuclear outages continued.

"Even if Connecticut Yankee and Millstone are not operational any time during the 1996-1997 winter season and the 1997 summer season, (peak demand will be met) so long as the remaining generating units in Connecticut and the New England region have normal operability," the company said.
It said "NU expects to continue incurring substantial costs during the rest of 1996 as a result of the Millstone outages, which could result in a loss for the fourth quarter.
"A key factory affecting 1996 earnings will be the level of costs expended to address Nuclear Regulatory Commission concerns" and replacement power costs, the company said.

The filing reiterated the estimate that incremental non-fuel operation and maintenance costs will be $147 million this year, of which about $108 million was spent in the first nine months of the year.
"It is likely that these costs will rise as NU and the NRC identify additional issues that need to be resolved," the company said. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
